name: aasb2_real_banded_colony
description:
The As above, So below II interop on a map their own generation built, rather than one banded after the fact.

WHY A SECOND AASB2 SCENARIO. aasb2_banded_overlay reconfigures an existing map's band component, which is cheap and deterministic and exercises the interop wiring. It cannot exercise their GENERATION: Patch_MapGenerator_GenerateMap only fires for a player Settlement's own map, and a fixture save's map was generated before any mod under test was loaded. SettleColony runs the real path, so this map has their real gutters, real carved bands and real see-through cells -- and costs a full map generation to get, which their own comment puts at roughly 3x normal.

The four state probes are the assertion. A map that silently failed to band still loads, still renders, and reads as an ordinary colony, so 'it ran' is not evidence of anything without them.

Clouds off, clock pinned: nothing here is testing either, and both drift between runs.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THIS THEIR GENERATION AND NOT SOMETHING ELSE. band_count 3 is their default level plan (one below, one above), and the map is 190 wide by 576 tall. SlotFor(190) = ceil(192/64)*64 = 192, and 3 * 192 = 576 exactly: the map's z is bandCount * SlotFor(width) while its width is untouched, which is the shape their Patch_MapGenerator_GenerateMap prefix inflates a map into and nothing else produces. All three are pinned at tolerance 0, so a settings change or a generation-path change fails here rather than quietly measuring an ordinary colony.
